title.narrative: The Neighbourhood Energy Investment Fund (NEIF) in Ukraine, 2017-2022

description.narrative:
Impact Fund Denmark (IFDK) is Denmark’s development finance institution, supporting sustainable private sector investments in developing countries. IFDK invests in sustainable growth and high-impact solutions, mobilising capital to tackle global challenges where the need is greatest. The focus is on investments that offer high development impact and scalable business opportunities.
The Danish support concerning NEIF is part of the Danish Neighbourhood Programme 2017-2021 and its pillar for sustainable and inclusive economic growth. NEIF cover both Georgia and Ukraine. The duration of the NEIF fund was initially 4 years to the end of 2021. It was prolonged with a year in 2022 due to the war in Ukraine and the mandate was extended to cover support to IFU’s existing projects which needed exceptional financing due to the fragile situation caused by the war.
Development effects of investments projects often take years to materialize, making them difficult to capture within short reporting periods. As a result, the indicator reporting focuses on tangible outputs, such as the number of investments, as proxies, based on the assumption that these will contribute to long-term development impact. To learn more about the development effects, see the case stories on IFDK’s website, in IFDK’s Annual Report, and in the Open Aid section below. The NEIF experience in Ukraine demonstrated that renewable energy projects are feasible and valuable. Early IFU investments helped pioneer Ukraine’s green transition, proving that private, commercial actors could operate in the sector despite significant legal uncertainty and later retroactive tariff cuts that undermined investor confidence. Developing new projects proved difficult due to regulatory changes, off taker payment delays, and the mismatch between NEIF criteria and typical Ukrainian energy efficiency project structures. The Neighbourhood Energy Investment Fund (NEIF) was launched in 2017 with the purpose of undertaking investments in sustainable energy projects in Ukraine and Georgia and thereby promote private investments, new technologies and know-how in the sector.
